https://www.euronews.com/2026/09/16/us-p.text: The US is planning to deliver a package of 40,000 powerful bombs to Israel as part of an upcoming arms deal. The $2.8 billion (€2.42 billion) deal includes 2,000-pound (900 kg) Mk84 and BLU-117 aircraft bombs, according to two US officials and a person familiar with the plan who spoke on condition of anonymity.The same weapons prompted concerns about the possibility of mass casualties in Gaza, and their delivery was put on hold by the the Biden administration two years ago. Trump lifted that hold when he took office again.Congress has been informally notified about the pending deal, most of which is to be paid for with foreign military financing — in which US taxpayer dollars are given to Israel to turn around and buy the weapons from the United States.The proposed deal is just the latest in a series of Trump administration steps to improve Israel's military capacity. The conflict in Gaza has left tens of thousands of Palestinians dead and has decimated the enclave. The US had brokered a fragile ceasefire, but violence has continued.The package, which was reported earlier by The Washington Post, comes as Israel has faced increasing international isolation over its war in Gaza in response to the deadly attacks by Hamas on 7 October 2023.The sale signals that while the relationship between President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is reportedly strained, the US-Israel military relationship has not significantly weakened.The two countries launched the war against Iran in February. Trump had expressed frustration with Netanyahu tied to the Iran conflict before their latest meeting in July at the White House.Last year, the Trump administration bypassed a normal congressional review process and approved a nearly $3 billion sale to Israel that included more than 35,500 of the bombs. The administration then approved a new series of arms sales to Israel totalling $6.67 billion in January.

Photograph: Ross D Franklin/AP Arizona A possible three tornados wallop Arizona, bringing golf-ball sized hail Violent storms overnight knocked over utility poles and trees and carried thunder and heavy winds through state Associated Press Thu 22 Oct 2026 19.15 EDT First published on Thu 22 Oct 2026 08.28 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Yet more severe weather struck Thursday in the US south-west as the Four Corners region surveyed blown-away roofs, trees knocked on to homes and power lines downed from overnight tornadoes that injured one person. The injuries weren’t life-threatening but rare for an area better known for scalding heat. But this fall has been unusually soggy in the south-west with El Niño conditions that have sent one tropical system after another in from the Pacific, causing the Grand Canyon and surrounding deserts to rage with floods. Now, golf ball-size hail and tornadoes have joined the mix. National Weather Service meteorologists suspect at least three tornadoes touched down as storms swept across central Arizona late Wednesday. The nasty weather hit during Lenna Landy’s yoga routine in Overgaard, a community of about 3,000 people 140 miles (225km) north-east of Phoenix. Landy had ignored alerts about a possible tornado, but then the storm struck. “It was like Zeus-was-angry kind of level, of thunder cracks,” Landy said. The power went off, her house shook and Landy couldn’t find her glasses. “If this is my end, I won’t see it coming,” she recalled thinking. “The scariest part was just like, how quickly it came on.” The storm peeled off nearby roofs, shattered windows and blew a shed into a home, she said. A spruce tree in her yard was split in half. View image in fullscreen A storm dumps heavy rain and hail across Flagstaff, Arizona, on Wednesday. Photograph: Cheyanne Mumphrey/AP Still more severe weather, including large hail, struck Thursday with much of Arizona under tornado and flood watches. Similar weather soaked New Mexico, while swathes of Utah and Colorado were under flood watches and warnings. Warm, moist air moving north fuels storms coming in from the California coast. Changing winds can make them spin, creating the conditions for tornadoes, said Ryan Bernhart, a weather service meteorologist in Flagstaff. “This is very unusual for this area at this time of the year,” Bernhart said. View image in fullscreen Uprooted trees cause damage at an apartment complex after storms hit the area on Wednesday in Mesa, Arizona. Photograph: Ross D Franklin/AP Tornadoes are somewhat but not exceptionally unusual in Arizona. Notable outbreaks happened in 2019 and 2010. Strong winds toppled trees in Flagstaff and Mesa, with some landing on walls and carports. A few dozen ponderosa pines more than 30ft (9 meters) tall fell down in the Coconino national forest, north-west of Flagstaff. “These are not small trees that are down,” Bernhart said. “These are pretty strong trees that had been knocked down.” Explore more on these topics Arizona US weather Tornadoes Extreme weather news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed US news US politics Midterms 2026 World Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine US immigration Soccer Business Environment Tech Science Newsletters The Filter Wellness
